Your job: black-box INVESTIGATE and DOCUMENT the JS-level behavior of the original's `require('zlib')` module (non-stream parts). Another engineer will implement the JS bindings purely from your report, so be concrete and exact (exact error names/messages/codes, exact return types, sample outputs).

HARD RULES: You may RUN /tmp/orig to observe behavior. You must NOT disassemble/decompile it, read its bytes (no strings/hexdump/objdump on it), use strace/ltrace or any tracing on it, and do NOT call Function.prototype.toString / String(fn) on zlib functions or classes to read their source. No internet. Do not write anything under /workspace (read-only for you); keep ALL your scratch files under /tmp/agent_a1/. Node v18 (/usr/bin/node) is available for comparison only — the ORIGINAL is the source of truth (it differs from node in many ways).

QUIRKS ALREADY KNOWN: `console.log` in this runtime prints values with plain String(v) (objects print as "[object Object]"), so print with JSON.stringify, Object.keys, Buffer#toString('hex') etc. The engine refuses typed arrays larger than 1 MiB (RangeError "Invalid typed array length"), so keep test data small. The codecs themselves are custom: e.g. `zlib.inflateSync(Buffer.from([1,2,3]))` throws a plain Error with message "zlib: input too short" and NO code/errno properties; gunzip ignores CRC/trailing data; all compression options (level, strategy, windowBits, dictionary, brotli params, zstd params) appear to be ignored by the compressors. You do not need to study the compressed byte format; focus on the JS API surface.

INVESTIGATE (for every exported function: deflateSync inflateSync gzipSync gunzipSync deflateRawSync inflateRawSync unzipSync brotliCompressSync brotliDecompressSync zstdCompressSync zstdDecompressSync, and the async ones deflate inflate gzip gunzip deflateRaw inflateRaw unzip brotliCompress brotliDecompress zstdCompress zstdDecompress, plus crc32):
1. Module surface: Object.keys(zlib) order; typeof of each export; fn.name and fn.length of every function; whether the class exports (Gzip, Deflate, ...) are functions/classes, callable without `new`, their .name/.length, prototype chain (e.g. instanceof require('stream').Transform? EventEmitter?). Is `zlib.constants` frozen / writable? `zlib.codes`? Any extra properties (e.g. zlib.default for ESM `import zlib from 'node:zlib'`, named ESM imports `import { gzipSync } from 'node:zlib'`).
2. Input types for each sync function: string (which encoding? try non-ASCII like "héllo€"), Buffer, Uint8Array, Uint16Array/Int32Array/Float64Array (does it use the underlying bytes incl. byteOffset/byteLength of a subarray view?), DataView, ArrayBuffer, SharedArrayBuffer (if available), number, boolean, null, undefined, plain object, array of numbers. Record exactly what is thrown (constructor name, e.name, e.message, e.code, Object.keys(e)) or what is returned.
3. Return value: Buffer.isBuffer(result)? instanceof Uint8Array? result.buffer byteLength vs result.length (is it a view into a bigger ArrayBuffer?). For empty input.
4. Options handling for each sync function: pass invalid values (level: 10, -2, 1.5, '6', NaN; windowBits: 7, 16, 0; memLevel 0/10; strategy 5/-1; chunkSize: 1, 63, 64; dictionary: 'string', 123, Buffer; maxOutputLength: 0, 1, 10, -1, 'x'; info: true; finishFlush: values; flush; params: {}/invalid keys/values for brotli & zstd; options = null/123/'str'). Does anything throw? With what error? Does `info: true` change the return (e.g. {buffer, engine})? Does maxOutputLength limit output (try decompressing data whose output exceeds it) and with what error?
5. Async callback forms: zlib.gzip(buf, cb), zlib.gzip(buf, opts, cb). Is the callback invoked synchronously or asynchronously (log order around the call, compare with process.nextTick / Promise.resolve().then / setTimeout(0) ordering)? Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. ASYNC CALLBACK FORMS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Applies to deflate inflate gzip gunzip deflateRaw inflateRaw unzip brotliCompress
brotliDecompress zstdCompress zstdDecompress. All behave identically; results equal the sync
versions (checked for all 11).
- Signatures: x(data, cb) and x(data, opts, cb). If the 2nd arg is a function (typeof ===
  'function', including a Proxy of a function), it becomes the callback and the 3rd arg is ignored.
  Otherwise the 3rd arg is the callback. (buf, undefined, cb), (buf, null, cb), (buf, 'str', cb)
  and (buf, 0, cb) all work.
- Return value is undefined. Nothing is ever thrown synchronously, not even for bad input,
  corrupt data or a missing callback.
- Timing: the whole job runs in ONE promise-reaction microtask scheduled at call time: input
  conversion, compression, then the callback. Ordering test, in registration order:
      promise-before, microtask-before, [zlib.gzip call], promise-after
      -> promise-before, microtask-before, gzip-cb, promise-after
  The callback runs before setTimeout(0), setImmediate and (in this runtime) process.nextTick.
  With a 4-step .then chain started before the call: "tick1 gzip-cb gunzip-err-cb tick2 tick3 tick4".
  Multiple calls complete FIFO. Node, by contrast, calls back in a later macrotask.
  Because the work is deferred, mutating the input after the call changes the result:
    b=Buffer.from('aaaa'); zlib.deflate(b, cb); b.fill(0x62)  -> result inflates to "bbbb"
    the same for a Uint16Array or an Array mutated after the call.
- Success: cb(null, resultBuffer). arguments.length is 2. `this` is undefined (strict callback)
  or globalThis (sloppy).
- Failure: cb(err). arguments.length is 1 (no second arg). err is the same object the sync
  function would throw:
    zlib.inflate(Buffer.from([1,2,3]), cb) -> cb(Error "zlib: input too short")
    zlib.gzip(5, cb)                       -> cb(TypeError "Buffer.from: unsupported value")
    zlib.gzip(undefined, cb)               -> cb(TypeError "Buffer.from: unsupported value")
- If the callback throws on success, it is called AGAIN with that exception
  (try { cb(null, r) } catch (e) { cb(e) }):
    zlib.gzip('x', (err) => { n++; if (n===1) throw new Error('boom') })
    -> call #1 err=null, call #2 err=Error 'boom'
  If the callback throws again (or throws in the error case), the promise rejects unhandled. The
  runtime prints "Uncaught (in promise) Error: boom #2" to STDERR. The process continues and exits
  0. process.on('unhandledRejection') and process.on('uncaughtException') handlers are NOT called.
- Missing or non-function callback: zlib.gzip('hello'), zlib.gzip('hello', {}),
  zlib.gzip('hello','notfn'), zlib.gzip('hello',{},5), zlib.gzip('hello', null), and also
  corrupt or invalid input without a callback, all return undefined without throwing. Later STDERR
  shows "Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: cb is not a function" and the exit code is 0.
  (The callback variable is literally named `cb`. That engine message comes from calling an
  undefined `cb`. Engine quirk: once the same call site has thrown 8 times, the engine changes it to
  "undefined is not a function"; plain JS reproduces this too, so it is not zlib logic.)
  Node instead throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE synchronously.
- util.promisify(zlib.gzip)('hello') returns a Promise that resolves to a Buffer. With corrupt
  input it rejects with the plain Error (e.g. "gzip: bad magic"). util.promisify(zlib.deflate)
  ('abc', {level: 9}) works. zlib.gzip[util.promisify.custom] is undefined. There is no
  zlib.promises.

7. DECOMPRESSOR ERRORS AND CODEC BEHAVIOR (all errors are plain Error with only "message" as own prop)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Each message is prefixed with the codec. Observed messages:
 inflateSync (zlib wrapper):
   length < 6 bytes                         -> "zlib: input too short"  (e.g. [], [0], [1,2,3])
   CM nibble (byte0 & 0x0f) != 8            -> "zlib: unsupported compression method" (garbage, ff.., gzip data, 7f9c)
   Not checked: FCHECK (789d accepted), CINFO (0800 accepted), FDICT, Adler-32 (missing, wrong or
   truncated trailer all accepted). The deflate stream is parsed from byte 2. Trailing junk and a
   second stream are ignored.
   inflate errors: "inflate: unexpected end of input", "inflate: invalid literal/length symbol",
   "inflate: distance too far back".
 inflateRawSync:
   []                                       -> "inflate: unexpected end of input"
   [0] or [1,2,3]                           -> "inflate: truncated stored block"
   '0123456789abcdef'                       -> "inflate: stored block overruns input"
   16 x 0xff                                -> "inflate: reserved block type"
   Stored-block NLEN is not checked against ~LEN. Trailing data is ignored.
 gunzipSync and unzipSync (identical):
   total length < 18 or magic != 1f8b       -> "gzip: bad magic"  (even a valid but truncated 17-byte gzip)
   CM != 8                                  -> "gzip: unsupported compression method"
   FEXTRA, FNAME, FCOMMENT and FHCRC are handled. Reserved flag bits are ignored.
   The deflate data is header..(len-8). The 8-byte trailer is stripped and NEVER checked (wrong
   CRC/ISIZE accepted). Losing trailer bytes therefore yields "inflate: unexpected end of input",
   while body + any 8 junk bytes works.
   Only the FIRST member is decoded: gzip('abc')+gzip('def') -> "abc" (Node gives "abcdef").
   unzipSync does NOT auto-detect the zlib format: unzipSync(deflateSync(x)) -> "gzip: bad magic".
 brotliDecompressSync:
   [], [0], [1,2,3]  -> "brotli: unexpected end of input"
   other messages seen: "brotli: non-zero padding bits", "brotli: uncompressed block overruns input",
   "brotli: corrupt code-length code", "brotli: reserved bit set".
   16 x 0xff -> returns an empty Buffer (no error). Trailing junk and a second stream are ignored.
 zstdDecompressSync:
   []                -> "zstd: empty input"
   [0] or [1,2,3]    -> "zstd: truncated frame"
   bad magic         -> "zstd: bad magic number" (trailing junk after a frame gives this too)
   others: "zstd: truncated raw block", "zstd: truncated content checksum",
   "zstd: content checksum mismatch".
   Two concatenated frames -> both outputs concatenated.

  - Later, stderr shows `Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: cb is not a function` and the exit code is 0. Node throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE immediately.
  - After the same call site has thrown 8 times, the engine changes the message to `"undefined is not a function"`. Plain JS shows the same quirk, so it is not zlib logic.
- **Promises:** `util.promisify(zlib.gzip)` works and rejects with the plain Error on bad input. There is no `util.promisify.custom` on these functions and no `zlib.promises`.

## 6. `zlib.crc32(data[, value])`
- **Algorithm and return:** standard CRC-32; every value matches Python's `zlib.crc32(bytes, value)`. Returns an unsigned 32-bit Number.
- **`data`:** follows the section 2 rule; strings are UTF-8.

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `crc32('hello')` | 907060870 |
| `crc32('')` | 0 |
| `crc32('héllo€')` | 464142983 |
| `crc32(new Uint16Array([0x6568]))` | 2439710439 (CRC of the single byte `0x68`) |
| `crc32(DataView)` | 0 |
| `crc32(new String('hello'))` | 3324180253 (five zero bytes) |
| `crc32(5)`, `crc32(null)`, `crc32()` | TypeError `"Buffer.from: unsupported value"` |

- **`value`:** converted like `value >>> 0`, with no validation. `valueOf` is called once.
  - Order: `data` is converted first, then `value`, then the native type check runs.

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `crc32('world', crc32('hello '))` | 222957957, same as `crc32('hello world')` |
| `crc32('hello', -1)` | 265137764, same as passing 4294967295 |
| `crc32('hello', 4294967296)`, or with NaN, Infinity, `'abc'` | 907060870 |
| `crc32('hello', 1.9)` or `true` | 191926070 |
| `crc32('', -1)` | 4294967295 |
| `crc32('', '0x10')` | 16 |
| `crc32('hello', 5n)` | TypeError `"Cannot mix BigInt and other types, use explicit conversions"` |
| `crc32('hello', Symbol())` | TypeError `"Cannot convert a Symbol value to a number"` |

- `new zlib.crc32('x')` throws TypeError `"object is not a constructor"`.

## 7. Decompressor errors
All are plain Error objects with no code or errno.

- **inflateSync:**
  - Input shorter than 6 bytes: `"zlib: input too short"`.
  - `(byte0 & 0x0f) != 8`: `"zlib: unsupported compression method"`.
  - Not checked: FCHECK, FDICT, Adler-32. Trailing junk is ignored.
- **inflateRawSync:**
  - Messages: `"inflate: unexpected end of input"`, `"inflate: truncated stored block"`, `"inflate: stored block overruns input"`, `"inflate: reserved block type"`, `"inflate: invalid literal/length symbol"`, `"inflate: distance too far back"`.
  - Stored-block NLEN is not checked.
- **gunzipSync and unzipSync** (identical):
  - Input shorter than 18 bytes or wrong magic: `"gzip: bad magic"`.
  - Bad compression method: `"gzip: unsupported compression method"`.
  - The header flags (FEXTRA, FNAME, FCOMMENT, FHCRC) are parsed correctly.
  - The last 8 bytes are stripped and never checked, so a truncated trailer gives `"inflate: unexpected end of input"`.
  - Only the first member of a multi-member gzip is decoded (Node returns all members).
  - `unzipSync(deflateSync(x))` throws `"gzip: bad magic"`.
- **brotliDecompressSync:**
  - Messages: `"brotli: unexpected end of input"`, `"brotli: non-zero padding bits"`, `"brotli: uncompressed block overruns input"`, `"brotli: corrupt code-length code"`, `"brotli: reserved bit set"`.
  - 16 bytes of `0xff` returns an empty Buffer.
- **zstdDecompressSync:**
  - Messages: `"zstd: empty input"`, `"zstd: truncated frame"`, `"zstd: bad magic number"` (also raised by trailing junk), `"zstd: truncated raw block"`, `"zstd: truncated content checksum"`, `"zstd: content checksum mismatch"`.
  - Concatenated frames decode to the concatenated output.

## 8. Differences from Node 18
- **Exports:** the original adds zstd and crc32 and uses a different key order. Its classes are lazy getters, and there are no top-level `Z_*` constants.
- **Functions and classes:** function names are `""`, classes are named `"cls"`, sync functions have length 1, and the classes require `new`. Instances lack close, flush, params and reset.
- **Constants and codes:** `constants` and `codes` are mutable. `Z_MAX_CHUNK` is `null`, `ZLIB_VERNUM` is 4865, and `codes` has a different key order.
- **Input conversion:**
  - Other typed arrays are converted element by element.
  - A DataView counts as empty.
  - Arrays and array-likes are accepted.
  - Bad types throw TypeError `"Buffer.from: unsupported value"` with no code.
- **Options:** never read, so there is no validation, `info`, `maxOutputLength`, `dictionary` or `finishFlush` support.
- **Errors and checks:**
  - Errors are plain Errors with codec-prefixed messages and no code or errno.
  - No checksum checks are done.
  - Only the first gzip member is decoded, and `unzip` handles gzip only.
- **Async:** completes in one microtask and reports every error through the callback. A missing callback becomes an unhandled rejection. A throwing callback is called twice.
